messages.text: BSB Bitaxe Gamma 602 (1.8TH/s) faulty power supply. udner volt 4.7v

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me.

A Gamma 602 reading 4.7V is a classic weak power brick, not a bad board. The A. wants a solid 5V at the barrel, and these units sag under load when the supply cannot hold current.

Two things to confirm, one at a time:

1. Where does the 4.7V come from, the Bitaxe web UI / screen reading, or a multimeter at the plug?
2. Does the unit still boot and hash at all, or does it reset / drop chips when it ramps up?

If you have another 5V supply around (5V, 4A or more, correct barrel polarity), plug it in and tell me what the voltage reads then. That single test tells us everything. Do not open the power supply or modify the cable.

I've logged this as a power supply fault so the team can get a replacement brick out to you. They pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.

For a faster answer in the meantime, our Discord is very active: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , ask for @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead).
Handed to the team · Needs a mailed part (new 5V power supply) which only the team can send.
That's logged with the team. Send me those two answers (where the 4.7V reading comes from, and whether it still boots and hashes) and I'll keep going from there.
axeos, not hashing power supply fault on the screen
Let me check what AxeOS reports for that exact message rather than guess.
Searched the web · AxeOS Bitaxe "power fault" screen message input voltage
Searched the web · esp-miner AxeOS POWER_FAULT voltage threshold github

Got it, that message is the TPS546 regulator latching off, and 4.7V at the input explains it. 
The T.546 only turns on around 4.8V, so an underpowered supply or thin cable that sags under load trips an undervoltage fault
, and 
the latch is held in the regulator's own status register until input power is physically removed, so a restart from the web UI or the reset button does not clear it
. Source: the ESP-Miner/AxeOS behaviour documented on GitHub and the Bitaxe troubleshooting references.

Two things to do now, in this order:

1. Cold power cycle. Unplug the barrel jack for a full 10 seconds, then plug back in. Nothing less clears the latch.
2. If the banner comes back, open AxeOS Settings and check Core Voltage. On the Gamma the regulator will not run below 1000 mV, and 
if an overheat event dropped it to 980 mV that value sticks in memory and AxeOS keeps shouting "check your PSU" even after reboots and PSU swaps; setting it back above 1000 mV clears it instantly
. Stock for the 602 is 1100 to 1200 mV at around 485 to 525 MHz.

Tell me what Core Voltage and Frequency it shows, and the input voltage reading after the cold power cycle. If the core voltage is already at stock and the input still reads 4.7V, it is the brick and the replacement is already logged.

Also: make sure it is powered from the barrel jack, not USB-C. 
USB-C on current Bitaxes is serial and flashing only, it cannot deliver enough current to power the ASIC.


The team picks up the power supply side tomorrow at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email. If you want a faster hand, our Discord is active around the clock: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , ask for @nullhashrate (JD).
